newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela and China to sign Orimulsion deals.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela and China to sign Orimulsion deals.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng will sign a deal with Venezuela on the supply of trademark boiler fuel Orimulsion to China and on a possible joint venture Orimulson production plant, the Venezuelan Foreign Ministry said.
Li is expected in Caracas Tuesday on the last leg of a South American tour that already took him to Chile and Brazil.

The ministry said in a statement the accords will be signed during meetings Li is scheduled to have Thursday afternoon before his departure from Venezuela with Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta and Carlos Borregales, President of Bitumenes de Orinoco (Bitor), a unit of state-run Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA).
The ministry said the agreement would be for a "feasibility study" on the plant. It gave no further details but Venezuela and China have been laying the ground for these deals for months.
Bitor started in August a series of Orimulsion test shipments to China's National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC), which agreed to buy a test run of 500,000 tonnes.
If the tests went well, the deal contemplated construction of an Orimulsion production plant in Venezuela with a capacity of 5,2 million tonnes per year.
That figure would represent about 25 percent of Venezuela's planned Orimulsion output by the end of the decade. It exported 3.6 million tonnes of the bitumen and water mix fuel in 1995.
CNPC President Wang Tao said during a visit to Caracas earlier this year the plant would cost up to $320 milion.
Orimulsion is produced from an extra heavy bitumen-type oil found in large quantities in northern Veenzuela.
Venezuela has already supplied contracts for the heavy fuel with power generators in the United States, United Kingdom, Japan, Norway, Denmark, Lithuania, Italy and Canada.
